title: A stale feedback.ids lock taken by two writers that both saw it stale can be held by both
goal: _take_ids_lock lets one of two takers that saw the same stale lock win: the other's read-back of the lock fails, as the rename path before BG-a7ocbxua did, so no feedback id is lost to two writers in the window

run:
import sys
def _fail(t, e, tb, _d=sys.excepthook):
    if issubclass(t, AssertionError):
        print("check failed:", e)
        sys.exit(1)
    _d(t, e, tb)
sys.excepthook = _fail
import os, pathlib, sys, tempfile, time
sys.path.insert(0, "_tools")
import ql_capture as q
d = pathlib.Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
lock = d / "feedback.ids.lock"
lock.write_text("")
old = time.time() - 3600
os.utime(lock, (old, old))
q.FEEDBACK_IDS_LOCK_WAIT_S = 0.3
real, fired, got = os.replace, [], {}
def replace(a, b, *r, **k):
    if not fired:
        fired.append(1)
        got["B"] = q._take_ids_lock(lock, "tokB")  # a second taker saw the same stale lock and took it first
    return real(a, b, *r, **k)
os.replace = replace
try:
    got["A"] = q._take_ids_lock(lock, "tokA")
finally:
    os.replace = real
assert fired, "the check never saw the first taker replace the lock"
assert not (got.get("A") and got.get("B")), ("two takers that saw the same stale lock both hold it", got, lock.read_text())
